newsitem.title: USA: Mystery writer's death remains a mystery.
newsitem.headline: Mystery writer's death remains a mystery.

text.p: Police Thursday continued to investigate the hanging death of mystery writer Eugene Izzi, with the FBI standing by willing to help examine the scores of clues left behind.
"We're not investigating, unless they need some technical help," FBI spokesman Bob Long said of the Chicago Police Department's probe.

Izzi, 43, was found hanging by a rope Saturday outside his downtown office window. He was wearing a bullet-proof vest, and carried in his pockets hundreds of dollars in cash, a set of brass knuckles, a few computer diskettes, and several handwritten notes. A handgun was found on a desk to which one end of the rope had been tied, and the office door was locked.

Various friends of the writer have intimated in published reports that he was an unlikely suicide given that he had a new book coming out soon and showed remarkable perseverence in a decade of modestly successful mystery writing.

Several friends said Izzi had told them his research had taken him into dangerous territory with militia groups in Indiana, and he had been threatened. Police said the notes Izzi carried detailed transcripts of the supposed threats.
Some theorised that Izzi, a one-time steelworker who was married with two teenaged sons, may have killed himself but purposely left an elaborate mystery behind.

Another Chicago-based mystery writer and friend, Paul Engleman, told the Wall Street Journal that Izzi may have been somewhat paranoid and had spoken of anonymous threats before, but he questioned whether Izzi would be driven to suicide. Izzi had published previous books under a pseudonym and without a photograph of himself on the jacket.
